newsitem.title: UK: Britain confident of settling Albanian gold issue.
newsitem.headline: Britain confident of settling Albanian gold issue.

text.p: The British government said on Monday it was confident that Albanian gold held at the Bank of England since being recovered from the Nazis during World War Two would be returned to Albania soon.

A high-level delegation headed by Albanian central bank governor Kristaq Luniku is due in London later on Monday and the $18 million-worth of gold will be on the agenda when the team begins talks at the Foreign Office on Tuesday.
"We're extremely hopeful of concluding the Albania gold question," a Foreign Office official said.
He said the talks would be on "technical issues" covering the eventual transfer of the gold to Albania from the Bank of England, where it has been held since 1947.
The gold is controlled by a tripartite commission set up by three of the wartime Allies, Britain, France and the United States.
Britain agreed in May 1992 to return the gold after resolving an unrelated diplomatic dispute involving the sinking of two British warships off the Albanian coast in 1946 with the loss of 44 lives.
As part of the deal, Albania agreed to pay compensation of about $2 million.
